walkthroughs.body_html:
From about 1908, the WSPU turned to more militant tactics.

Suffragettes smashed shop windows, set fire to empty buildings and even attacked paintings in galleries.

They were arrested by the hundred and sent to prisons like Holloway. Newspapers gave them more attention than ever. 📰

In prison, suffragettes refused to eat — hunger strikes.

The government feared a death in custody. So prisons started force-feeding them with tubes. The process was painful and shocked the public.

The 1913 Cat and Mouse Act let the government release weak hunger strikers, then re-arrest them once they were well again.

On 4 June 1913, suffragette Emily Davison stepped onto the racetrack at the Epsom Derby, in front of the King's horse Anmer.

She was struck and died of her injuries four days later. Many think she was trying to attach a 'Votes for Women' flag to the king's horse.

Her funeral became a huge suffragette march. To many she was a martyr; to others her death seemed shocking and pointless. 🌷

mcqs.q: What caused the First World War?
options: Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
Wannsee was the meeting where Hitler personally launched WWII.
The assassination of Archduke Franz Ferdinand caused the war.
Long-term tensions (militarism, alliances, imperialism, nationalism) combined with the July Crisis triggered by the assassination of Franz Ferdinand.

mcqs.q: How effective was Nazi propaganda in winning popular support?
options: Germany declared war on Britain to seize colonies.
Goebbels invented television specifically to broadcast Nazi propaganda.
Nazi propaganda was so powerful that Germans believed whatever Hitler said.
Most effective where it reinforced existing views (anti-Versailles, fear of communism, national pride); less so when contradicting daily experience or established religious belief.

mcqs.q: What did the Wannsee Conference of January 1942 decide?
options: It coordinated the bureaucracy of the already-decided Final Solution across ministries, scaling existing mass murder into a systematic Europe-wide extermination programme.
Wannsee was the meeting where Hitler personally launched WWII.
Goebbels invented television specifically to broadcast Nazi propaganda.
Wannsee was the meeting where the Nazis first decided to murder all Jews.
